title: Leaving McKinney in 1932 and the personnel shuffle
summary: He stayed until about May 1932; Redman left to form his own band, Carter took over, and Rex Stewart, Hilton Jefferson and others came and went.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: How long did you stay with that band then, Brother?

Well, I stayed with that band from December 7, 1930, to about May 1932. And there was a little discrepancy in the band then. Don had left the band and Bennie Carter came but Bennie wasn't that interested in the band either. So Bennie did some writing and all that. So Rex Stewart had come with the band at the time. Buddy Lee had left and went to New York with Don.

So Rex left and went to New York and he called me back and he said, "Fletcher would like to have you in his band." He said, "Why don't you come to New York?" So Bennie Carter was going, coming to New York, too, he and Hilton Jefferson because Hilton Jefferson was in the band, in McKinney's band at the time, too.
Is that so? Hilton Jefferson in the band?
Oh, sure.
I didn't know that.
He come in when Inge left. You see,
Inge came to New York with Don.
I see. So tell me about that switch. Now, when Inge left Hilton Jefferson took Inge's place in the McKinney's Cottonpickers band?
That's right, that's right.
And when Don Redman left, Bennie Carter --
Bennie Carter came over, you see.
I see, uh-huh.
When the switch first started, first, Cuppy had left and they had sent and got Big Green in Cuppy's place, Charlie --
(trombone player,)
Big Green, Charlie Green.
Yeah, see. And they got Doc Cheatham in Langston Curl's place because Langston went to New York with Don, see. And Buddy Lee went to New York with Don, you see?
Uh-huh.
So that's when they got Rex. But Joe Smith stayed with McKinney, --
I see.
-- you see? And later on Cuppy came back because Big Green didn't stay. And Bennie Carter took Don's place in front of the band.
Right.
But --
